habitat: A dry inland bird of open arid bushveld. It avoids forest, dense bush and high mountains, and prefers well-drained stony or gravelly ground with sparse leaf litter, usually near trees or bushes.
summary: A breeding summer migrant, 23–24 cm. Wikipedia says the plumage is similar to the Fiery-necked Nightjar and gives the size, but it does not list the colours, so none were stored. SABAP1 shows a clear peak from late August to early April and says it is largely absent in winter, May to August.

similar.note: Fiery-necked Nightjar uses moister, more wooded ground and is resident in the lowveld. Rufous-cheeked Nightjar prefers open arid bush and is largely gone in winter.

viewNotes.note: Plumage colours were not listed in the texts used. It rests on dry, stony ground near bushes.

calls.description: No call was described in the Wikipedia or SABAP1 texts consulted. The file is a grade A call from near Klerksdorp, North West. The filename is RC Nightjar.

research.note: Newman has no page. Months are August to April. SABAP1 says late August to early April, and largely absent May to August. Plumage colours were not copied from the Fiery-necked Nightjar, because the text only says the two are similar. The call description is a gap. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
